title: Fair GPU Lease Orchestrator with KV Prioritization and SLO-tiered Grace Periods
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lease-based GPU allocation orchestrator that enforces SLO-tiered grace periods and KV cache prioritization to improve fairness and reduce tail latency for continuous batching workloads.
background: We currently rely on coarse preemption heuristics that either aggressively evict KV entries or abruptly interrupt tenant slices, which increases tail latency and causes unnecessary cold-cache penalties. As workload mix diversifies (short low-latency queries vs long generation requests with large KV working sets) we need a coordinated approach that treats GPU memory (model weights + KV) and compute slices as unified leases. This ticket designs and implements an orchestrator that issues time-boxed GPU leases with SLO-tiered grace periods and a KV prioritization policy to shepherd hot working sets through preemption events.
proposal: Introduce a 'lease' abstraction: each active slice receives a lease with (duration, kv_pin_budget, grace_level). Leases are issued by the orchestrator based on tenant SLO score, recent observed P95/P99 latency, and fair-share weights. When GPU pressure is detected, the orchestrator executes a 3-stage grace pipeline: (1) gentle reclaim - request voluntary shrink/early termination with KV shadow eviction hints; (2) soft-preempt - pause slice and attempt to checkpoint minimal KV deltas to a fast local slab; (3) hard-preempt - preempt and evict heavy KV segments but preserve pins for top-N hot keys. KV prioritization uses an LRU+hotscore where hotscore is a moving average combining access frequency and SLO criticality. The orchestrator exposes tunables for grace durations per SLO tier, kv_pin_budget per lease, and a fast-path reclamation RPC for the runtime to release non-hot KV pages immediately.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Initial design proposal drafted and reviewed with runtime owners. Raised concerns about checkpointing latency for large KV deltas.
2026-03-11: Microbenchmarks: simulated 50/50 short/long workload mix. Lease allocator prototype reduced preempt hard events by 37% and P99 by 12% in simulation (see dashboard link).

2026-03-12: Design review with storage team — agreed on a bounded async slab for KV delta buffering to avoid synchronous disk IO in preempt path. Action: add eviction telemetry and fast checksum for delta validity.
2026-03-13: Spike PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/492). Runtime changes stubbed: lease API + reclamation RPC. Integration tests queued.
Next: implement KV hotscore aggregator and integrate with existing cache manager; add scheduler policy selector to route by tenant SLO when issuing leases.
decisions: Use lease abstraction instead of immediate token-slice preemption to reduce thrashing.
KV retention priorities will be computed from hotscore = 0.7*frequency + 0.3*recency adjusted by tenant_slo_multiplier.
Checkpointing of KV deltas will be async into a bounded in-memory slab with eviction tiers; no sync disk writes on the critical path.
Expose grace_level buckets (gold/silver/bronze) mapped directly from customer SLO tiers; default mapping set by product but overridable by enterprise policies.

acceptance_criteria: Deployed lease manager in canary runtime pool with feature flag off by default.
Simulated workloads show <=10% regression in throughput but >=15% reduction in hard-preempt events under mixed workloads.
P99 latency improved or unchanged for gold-tier tenants in canary compared to baseline.
No synchronous disk writes introduced on the hot path; measured increase in async slab memory < 8%.
Dashboard shows correct metrics and alerting for lease runaway and KV eviction spikes.
Security review completed for new lease RPC surface.
metrics: lease_churn_rate: leases per minute per GPU
hard_preempt_count: number of hard preempt events per hour
soft_preempt_count: number of soft preempt events per hour
kv_cold_miss_penalty: average additional latency for requests that hit cold KV after eviction
risks: Async KV delta buffering could grow unexpectedly for pathological workloads causing OOM in slab (mitigation: hard cap + backpressure).
Lease heuristics might unfairly favor older tenants if weights are not normalized (mitigation: include decay and recent activity in weight comp).
Incorrect hotscore tuning could cause hot keys to be evicted; requires careful A/B tuning and canary rollout.
Additional RPC surface increases attack surface—needs auth+narrow scopes for lease endpoints.
test_plan: Unit tests for lease lifetime logic and grace transitions.
Integration tests: simulate preemption pipeline (gentle -> soft -> hard) and validate KV correctness after checkpoint+restore.
Load test: 500 concurrent tenants with mixed SLOs to validate performance and slab cap enforcement.
Canary rollout on 5% of hosted region capacity for 48 hours with automated rollback if P99 for gold tier increases >5%.
Chaos test: randomly trigger forced reclaim and ensure no silent data corruption in KV slab.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy manager and runtime hooks in canary cluster (internal tenants only).
Phase 2: enable for low-risk tenant subset (beta customers) and monitor metrics for 7 days.
Phase 3: widen to 25% of traffic and tune hotscore parameters via runtime flags.
Phase 4: general availability and expose SLO-grace mappings in Console policies.
